description.value: Bearpaw Heli-Skiing is a boutique, owner-operated heli-ski operation based out of the handbuilt Binchi Lodge near Sinclair Mills, accepting just eight guests per week across 1.2 million acres of exclusive terrain spanning four mountain ranges. Named by Outside Magazine as one of the Coolest Backcountry Lodges, it is guided exclusively by ACMG- and CSGA-certified professionals flying AStar B3 helicopters. The operation is entirely winter-season and package-based, with no walk-in or drop-in access.

address.value: 37763 Upper Fraser Road, Sinclair Mills BC, Canada, V0J 3M0

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website is fully accessible and confirms this is an owner-operated heli-skiing lodge (Binchi Lodge) near Sinclair Mills, BC, catering exclusively to small-group winter ski packages. The site contains no mention of bicycles, bike storage, cycling infrastructure, or any amenity relevant to touring cyclists. One discrepancy flagged: the contact page shows '1-866-500-HELI' (=1-866-500-4354) while the site footer consistently shows TF: 1.866.550.4354 — these differ at the 550/500 digit. OSM had no phone or address, so contact_confirmed for those fields is null.
concerns: Toll-free number discrepancy: contact page displays '1-866-500-HELI' (1-866-500-4354) while site footer and other pages show TF: 1.866.550.4354 — one of these may be a typo.
This is a winter heli-skiing resort with no evident relevance to cycling tourism; no bicycle-related amenities or services mentioned anywhere on the site.
Seasonal and package-only operation — not an accessible drop-in accommodation for passing cyclists.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, operational, publicly bookable business with an active website; not permanently closed or a phantom listing. No cycling-specific amenities are confirmed, but that is not grounds for exclusion.
enrichment_extras.notes: OSM record lacked phone and address; both sourced from website. The business currently has availability opening for 2028 season (as of May 2026), consistent with a short winter season model.
